# Hadron MCP tools

<!-- Generated by `go run ./cmd/toolsdoc` from the action registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

Hadron serves 150 tools, one per action. Everything you can do in the app is also a tool, so a Claude
that you connect can drive the board the way you do. Tools marked **changes data** write to the
store; the others only read. See the README for how to connect.

Groups: [app](#app) (6), [card](#card) (11), [chat](#chat) (4), [client](#client) (1), [column](#column) (5), [config](#config) (3), [custom](#custom) (4), [dash](#dash) (8), [debug](#debug) (1), [diagnostics](#diagnostics) (1), [field](#field) (1), [filter](#filter) (2), [gate](#gate) (3), [integration](#integration) (16), [launch](#launch) (4), [link](#link) (6), [logs](#logs) (1), [planner](#planner) (8), [prompt](#prompt) (4), [question](#question) (5), [remote](#remote) (5), [rule](#rule) (7), [script](#script) (11), [session](#session) (10), [ui](#ui) (3), [update](#update) (4), [view](#view) (4), [widget](#widget) (2), [workspace](#workspace) (8), [worktree](#worktree) (2)

## app

### `app_status`

Report the running Hadron version, its data folder, how many actions exist and the database schema version.

*reads*

No arguments.

### `mcp_calls`

List the newest tool calls, newest first: who called (you, planner, session:<nick>, external, rule:<name>), which tool, the arguments, the outcome and the duration. Reads from the UI are not logged.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | only this workspace's calls; empty lists every workspace |
| `limit` | number | no | how many of the newest calls to return (default 100, at most 500) |

### `mcp_info`

Report where the Hadron MCP server listens, its bearer token, how many tools it serves and the command that connects your own Claude Code to it.

*reads*

No arguments.

### `notify`

Show a notification in the app: a toast for the user.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | yes | the notification title |
| `body` | string | no | the notification text |

### `settings_get`

Read global settings: one by key, or all.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | no | one setting; omit for all |

### `settings_update`

Change global settings, such as theme (light, dark or system). Returns all settings.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `values` | object | yes | setting keys and their new JSON values, for example {"theme": "dark"} |

## card

### `card_archive`

Archive a card so it leaves the board, or restore it with archived: false.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card_id` | string | yes | the card id |
| `archived` | boolean | no | true (default) to archive, false to restore |

### `card_chips`

For every card of a workspace, the values of the fields that are set to show as chips on the card face (custom fields and integration fields with card_chip on, such as jira.status). Cards with nothing to show are left out.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `card_create`

Create a card at the bottom of a column and start its Claude Code session, unless start is false. The nickname must be kebab-case and unique in the workspace. The launch profile decides the session's first prompt; none means no first prompt.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `nick` | string | yes | a kebab-case nickname, unique in the workspace, such as billing-fix |
| `key` | string | no | an optional key such as ACME-508 |
| `title` | string | no | an optional longer title |
| `column_id` | string | no | the column; defaults to the first active column |
| `assignee` | string | no | who owns the card; defaults to You |
| `launch_profile` | string | no | the launch profile for its session |
| `start` | boolean | no | start the card's session (default true) |

### `card_delete`

Delete a card with its sessions, questions, gates and links. This cannot be undone; prefer card_archive.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card_id` | string | yes | the card id |

### `card_field_set`

Set one field of a card. Native fields (card.assignee, card.stage, card.key, card.nick, card.column) and custom.* fields are written here; a field of a linked integration is written through the integration. Rules that watch the field run afterwards.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card` | string | yes | the card: id, nickname or key |
| `path` | string | yes | the field: card.assignee, card.stage, card.key, card.nick, card.column, custom.<name> or <integration>.<field>; field_schema_get lists them |
| `value` | object | yes | the new value: a string, number or true/false matching the field's type; an empty string clears it |

### `card_fields_get`

Read every field value of a card, keyed by path (card.column, custom.priority, jira.status...). Fields with no value yet read as an empty string, 0 or false.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card` | string | yes | the card: id, nickname or key |

### `card_get`

Get one card by id, with its column, liveness and fields.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card_id` | string | yes | the card id |

### `card_list`

List a workspace's cards in board order, optionally by column, role or liveness.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `column_id` | string | no | only cards in this column |
| `role` | string | no | only cards in columns with this role |
| `liveness` | string | no | working, idle, waiting or ended |
| `expr` | string | no | a CEL filter expression over the card, custom and integration fields, such as card.stage == 'review'; see field_schema_get |
| `include_archived` | boolean | no | also list archived cards |

### `card_move`

Move a card to a column, at a position (0 is the top; default is the bottom). Also reorders within a column.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card_id` | string | yes | the card id |
| `column_id` | string | yes | the destination column |
| `position` | number | no | 0 is the top of the column; default is the bottom |

### `card_report`

Report progress, a question, a blocker or completion on a card. It is stored on the card's channel and typed into the planner as "[KEY nick] report <kind>: <first 200 characters>". A session reports on its own card; so may the user.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card` | string | no | the card (id, nickname or key); a session reports on its own card and may leave this out |
| `kind` | string | yes | progress, question, blocked or done |
| `text` | string | yes | what to tell the planner and the user |

### `card_update`

Change a card's nickname, key, title, assignee, stage or launch profile. Use card_move to change its column.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card_id` | string | yes | the card id |
| `nick` | string | no | new kebab-case nickname |
| `key` | string | no | new key |
| `title` | string | no | new title |
| `assignee` | string | no | new assignee |
| `stage` | string | no | a short stage label |
| `launch_profile` | string | no | new launch profile |

## chat

### `chat_list`

List the channels that have messages: the planner's and each card's, with the message count and the newest message.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `chat_post`

Post the planner's reply on a channel. Only the planner (or the user, in tests) may call it. The post is stored; it is not typed anywhere.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `channel` | string | yes | planner, or card:<card id, nickname or key> |
| `text` | string | yes | the message; control characters are stripped and it is cut at 8,000 characters |

### `chat_read`

Read a channel's messages, oldest first. Optionally only those after a time, or only the newest few.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `channel` | string | yes | planner, or card:<card id, nickname or key> |
| `since` | string | no | only messages after this RFC 3339 time |
| `limit` | number | no | keep only the newest N messages (default: all) |

### `chat_send`

Send a message as the user. On a card's channel it is typed into the planner as "[KEY nick] text"; on the planner channel as "[planner] text". Only the user may call it; the planner answers with chat_post.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `channel` | string | yes | planner, or card:<card id, nickname or key> |
| `text` | string | yes | the message; control characters are stripped and it is cut at 8,000 characters |

## client

### `client_log`

Record an error from the app window in Hadron's log (the window calls this from its error handlers). Errors are always kept; lower levels only while debug logging is on.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `level` | string | yes | error, warn, info or debug |
| `message` | string | yes | what went wrong in the window |
| `stack` | string | no | the stack trace, if there is one |

## column

### `column_create`

Add a column at the end of the board.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `name` | string | yes | the column name |
| `role` | string | no | needs-you, active, blocked, done or backlog; rules use the role, never the name |
| `wip` | number | no | work-in-progress limit; 0 means no limit |
| `color` | string | no | a #rrggbb colour |

### `column_delete`

Delete a column. Its cards move to move_to, or to the first other column. A workspace keeps at least one column.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `column_id` | string | yes | the column to delete |
| `move_to` | string | no | the column that takes its cards; defaults to the first other column |

### `column_list`

List a workspace's columns in board order.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `column_reorder`

Set the order of the board's columns. Pass every column id of the workspace exactly once.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `column_ids` | array | yes | every column id of the workspace, in the new order |

### `column_update`

Rename a column or change its role, WIP limit, fold state or colour. A rename keeps the column's id, so rules and cards keep pointing at it.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `column_id` | string | yes | the column id |
| `name` | string | no | new name |
| `role` | string | no | new role, or an empty string for none |
| `wip` | number | no | new WIP limit; 0 means no limit |
| `fold` | boolean | no | fold the column to a narrow strip |
| `color` | string | no | new #rrggbb colour |

## config

### `config_diff`

Show what one config change changed: each field with its value before and after.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `change_id` | string | yes | the id from config_history |

### `config_history`

List the newest config changes of a workspace, newest first: who made each (you, planner, external, session:<nick>, rule:<name>), what, a one-line summary, and whether it can still be reverted. Covers workspaces, columns, rules, views, the dashboard, prompts, launch profiles and scripts. Pass actor to filter.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `limit` | number | no | how many of the newest changes (default 50, at most 500) |
| `actor` | string | no | only changes by this actor: you, planner, external, session, rule, or an exact one such as session:billing-fix or rule:Done moves |

### `config_revert`

Undo one config change by putting its before-state back. The revert is itself a change in the history. Refused, with the reason, when the thing has changed since (so a later edit is never silently overwritten), when it is not a config change, or when it was already reverted. Revert the newest change first to unwind several.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `change_id` | string | yes | the id from config_history |

## custom

### `custom_field_create`

Add a custom field to a workspace. It appears as custom.<name> in filters, rules and on cards.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `name` | string | yes | lowercase name, letters digits and underscores; the field becomes custom.<name> |
| `label` | string | no | the name shown in the UI |
| `type` | string | no | text, number, enum, user, date or bool; default text |
| `options` | array | no | the allowed values of an enum |
| `card_chip` | boolean | no | show the value as a chip on the card |

### `custom_field_delete`

Delete a custom field and clear its value on every card. This cannot be undone through the UI; config_revert restores the definition, not the values.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `name` | string | yes | the field's name, with or without the custom. prefix |

### `custom_field_list`

List a workspace's custom fields.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `custom_field_update`

Change a custom field's label, enum options or card chip. The type cannot change; delete the field and create it again for that.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `name` | string | yes | the field's name, with or without the custom. prefix |
| `label` | string | no | new label |
| `options` | array | no | new enum options |
| `card_chip` | boolean | no | show the value as a chip on the card |

## dash

### `dash_block_add`

Add one block to the dashboard. A stats, bars, heatmap, table or activity block needs a source query; prose needs text; planner blocks are written by the planner with dash_block_update; custom blocks take HTML.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `type` | string | yes | stats, bars, table, heatmap, prose, planner, activity or custom |
| `title` | string | yes | the block's heading |
| `span` | number | no | 1 for half width, 2 for full width; default 1 |
| `source` | object | no | the named query, its args and options. dash_get lists the queries |
| `html` | string | no | custom: the widget's HTML, rendered in a sandboxed frame with no network |
| `text` | string | no | prose or planner: the text |
| `schedule` | string | no | planner: hourly or daily HH:MM; empty to write only on demand |
| `position` | number | no | where to put it, 0 for first; default last |

### `dash_block_move`

Move a block to a place in the dashboard's order (0 is first).

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `block_id` | string | yes | the block id from dash_get |
| `position` | number | yes | the new place, 0 for first |

### `dash_block_refresh`

Refresh a block. A data block reruns its query and returns the result. A planner block types an instruction into the planner's session, asking it to write a short summary with dash_block_update; that costs the planner a turn, so it only happens when you ask (or on the block's own schedule).

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `block_id` | string | yes | the block id from dash_get |

### `dash_block_remove`

Remove a block from the dashboard.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `block_id` | string | yes | the block id from dash_get |

### `dash_block_update`

Change a dashboard block. Pass only what changes. A planner block's text is written this way, which stamps the time. The result is checked as a whole, so a change that makes the block invalid is refused with every problem.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `block_id` | string | yes | the block id from dash_get |
| `title` | string | no | new heading |
| `span` | number | no | 1 or 2 |
| `source` | object | no | new source; replaces the old one |
| `html` | string | no | custom: new HTML |
| `text` | string | no | prose or planner: new text. For a planner block this is how the planner writes its summary |
| `schedule` | string | no | planner: hourly, daily HH:MM, or empty |

### `dash_get`

Read the workspace's dashboard: each block with its data already resolved by its named query, and the queries available. Block types: stats, bars, table, heatmap, prose, planner, activity, custom.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `dash_query_run`

Run a named dashboard query now and return its result. cards.count{by,expr} gives groups; cards.list{expr}, questions.open, mcp.calls{since,by} and rules.fired{since} give rows (or groups); an integration adds <integration>.links and <integration>.count{by}.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `query` | string | yes | a named query: cards.count, cards.list, questions.open, mcp.calls, rules.fired or <integration>.links / <integration>.count |
| `args` | object | no | the query's arguments, such as {"by": "column"} |

### `dash_set`

Replace the whole dashboard with the given blocks, in order. Every problem is listed at once; nothing changes unless all blocks are valid. The history keeps the old layout.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `blocks` | array | yes | the whole dashboard, in order. Replaces the current blocks |

## debug

### `debug_logging_set`

Turn debug logging on or off. On, Hadron writes JSON lines at debug level to its log folder (7 days kept, 50 MB at most); off, only errors and recovered panics. Secrets, tokens and message text are never written either way.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | true writes debug-level lines to the log; false keeps only errors and panics |

## diagnostics

### `diagnostics_get`

Everything useful in a bug report: the version, macOS version, data and log folders, whether debug logging is on, the settings that cannot hold a secret, and the last 300 lines of the log.

*reads*

No arguments.

## field

### `field_schema_get`

List every field a card can have in a workspace: native card.* fields, the workspace's custom.* fields, and the fields of its enabled integrations. Filters and rules use these paths in CEL, such as card.stage == 'review'.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

## filter

### `filter_bar_set`

Choose which fields are pinned as chips in the board's filter bar. Only filterable fields can be pinned.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `fields` | array | yes | the field paths pinned as chips in the filter bar, in order; field_schema_get lists the filterable ones |

### `filter_eval`

Return the ids of the cards that satisfy a CEL expression, and optionally pinned field values (vals) and a text search (q), all of which must hold. A compile error comes back verbatim, with the position. An empty filter matches every card.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `expr` | string | no | a CEL expression, such as card.assignee == 'You' && custom.priority == 'high'; field_schema_get lists the fields |
| `vals` | object | no | pinned filters: each field path mapped to the value it must equal |
| `q` | string | no | only cards whose nickname, key or title contains this text |
| `include_archived` | boolean | no | also test archived cards |

## gate

### `gate_clear`

Clear a gate once the user has done or declined it. The user may always clear it; the planner only under the allow_all policy. A session can never clear its own gate.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gate_id` | string | no | the gate id; or pass card and kind |
| `card` | string | no | the card (id, nickname or key), with kind |
| `kind` | string | no | merge, promote, deploy-confirm or close, with card |

### `gate_list`

List the gates waiting on the user, oldest first, optionally for one card.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `card` | string | no | only this card's gates (id, nickname or key) |

### `gate_set`

Mark that a merge, promote, deploy-confirm or close on your card waits for the user. The card moves to Needs you until the gate is cleared. Setting the same kind again updates its summary.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card` | string | no | the card; a session sets a gate on its own card and may leave this out |
| `kind` | string | yes | merge, promote, deploy-confirm or close |
| `summary` | string | yes | what waits on the user, in one line |

## integration

### `integration_approve`

Approve a integration: its tests must pass, then it runs with the permissions its manifest lists. The user may always approve. The planner may unless the planner policy is decisions_only or ask_for_prd and the integration asks for network access, an MCP server or a binary that nothing approved already has. A card session never approves.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration or script name |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `integration_config_set`

Set an integration's settings (the config keys its manifest lists, such as a Jira site). Secrets such as API tokens go through integration_secret_set instead.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration name |
| `config` | object | yes | setting values by key; keys not listed keep their value |

### `integration_disable`

Switch an enabled integration off (it keeps its files and links), or reject a pending one.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration or script name |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `integration_list`

List the integrations visible to a workspace (its own and the global ones) with status (pending, enabled, disabled, rejected), permissions, what they ask for that nothing approved has, test results, settings and whether each secret is set. Secret values are never returned.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `integration_logs`

What integrations did lately, newest first: each op run with its duration, whether it worked, the error if not, and the lines the code logged. Secret values never appear.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | no | only this integration or script; empty for all |
| `limit` | number | no | how many rows, newest first; default 100 |

### `integration_read_file`

Read manifest.json or index.js of a integration.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration or script name |
| `path` | string | yes | manifest.json or index.js |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `integration_remove`

Delete a integration, its logs, its stored secrets and the links to its items. This cannot be undone through the UI; config_revert restores the files only.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration or script name |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `integration_run_op`

Run one op of an enabled integration for real (this uses its network access, secrets and binaries). Input and output are checked against the op's schema.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration or script name |
| `op` | string | yes | search, get, update, poll, actions.<name> or sessions.<list\|output\|send\|start\|stop> |
| `input` | object | no | the op's input object |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `integration_scaffold`

Create a new integration from a starter template, as pending. It does nothing until its tests pass and it is approved. Edit it with integration_write_file.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | lowercase name, letters digits and underscores; for an integration it is also the field namespace (jira gives jira.status) |
| `template` | string | no | integration_scaffold: linear (through the Linear MCP server), jira (REST), github (the gh CLI) or empty; default empty |
| `global` | boolean | no | make it available to every workspace instead of only this one |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `integration_secret_clear`

Delete a stored secret of an integration.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration name |
| `secret` | string | yes | the secret's name |

### `integration_secret_set`

Store a secret an integration uses (an API token). It goes to the macOS login keychain under the service "Hadron secrets" and is never shown or returned again.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration name |
| `secret` | string | yes | the secret's name, as listed in the manifest's permissions.secrets |
| `value` | string | yes | the secret value. Stored in the macOS keychain, never shown again |

### `integration_templates`

List the starter templates integration_scaffold accepts.

*reads*

No arguments.

### `integration_test`

Run the integration's recorded tests (manifest.tests). Each test calls an op with the network, exec and MCP answered by its fixtures, never the real thing, and compares the output with expect. The result is saved on the integration.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration or script name |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `integration_use`

Switch an approved integration on or off for one workspace. Its fields appear in filters, rules and cards only where it is on.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration name |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes | switch it on or off for the workspace |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `integration_validate`

Check a integration without running it: the manifest against its JSON Schema, the code parses, and every op the manifest declares is defined in the code.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration or script name |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `integration_write_file`

Replace manifest.json or index.js of a integration. The manifest is checked against its JSON Schema (every problem is listed) and the code must parse. An edit that keeps the same permissions re-runs the recorded tests and, if they pass, leaves an approved integration enabled; an edit that asks for more makes it pending again and needs approval.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration or script name |
| `path` | string | yes | manifest.json or index.js |
| `content` | string | yes | the whole new file |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

## link

### `link_action_run`

Run one of an integration's actions on a linked item, such as commenting on a Jira issue. The list of actions is in integration_list.

| `input` | object | no | extra input for the action; item_id is filled in |

### `link_add`

Link an item of an integration to a card. The integration's get op fetches its fields, which then appear as <integration>.<field> in filters, rules and on the card. Rules that watch those fields run.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |

| `card` | string | yes | the card: id, nickname or key |

| `url` | string | no | link to the item |

| `card` | string | yes | the card: id, nickname or key |

Re-read linked items from their integration now, instead of waiting for the next poll. Pass a link_id, or a card to refresh all of its links. Rules that watch a field that changed run.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |

| `link_id` | string | no | refresh this link |

Remove a link from its card. The item itself is untouched.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |

| `q` | string | yes | what to look for: a key, or words from the title |

## logs

### `logs_tail`

Read the newest lines of Hadron's own log (JSON lines under the logs folder in the data folder), oldest first. Without debug logging the log holds only errors and recovered panics. Secrets and message text are never logged.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lines` | number | no | how many of the newest lines (default 200, at most 2000) |
| `level` | string | no | only this level and above: debug, info, warn or error |
| `contains` | string | no | only lines that contain this text, ignoring case |

## planner

### `planner_adopt`

Make an existing Claude Code conversation the workspace's planner: Hadron resumes it with claude --resume, with the planner prompt and MCP server attached. Refused while the planner runs (stop it first) or if another Hadron card holds the conversation. Exit that conversation in its terminal first: two processes resuming one Claude Code conversation corrupt it.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `claude_session_id` | string | yes | the conversation's id from session_adoptable_list |
| `handoff` | boolean | no | type the planner handoff message once it is ready (default true) |

### `planner_get`

Report the workspace planner's session: whether it runs, its liveness, process id and terminal size.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `planner_policy_get`

Report the planner policy: allow_all (the planner may answer everything), decisions_only (it may answer decisions and unblocks, not approvals) or ask_for_prd (it may answer approvals that target DEV, not PRD).

*reads*

No arguments.

### `planner_policy_set`

Set the planner policy. Only the user can: the planner cannot widen its own permissions.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `policy` | string | yes | allow_all, decisions_only or ask_for_prd |

### `planner_read_screen`

Read what the planner's terminal shows, as plain text: the last lines (default 60), optionally with the scrollback.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `lines` | number | no | how many lines from the bottom (default 60) |
| `scrollback` | boolean | no | include lines that scrolled off the top |

### `planner_restart`

Stop the planner's session if it runs and start it again, resuming its conversation when that is known.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | start a new conversation instead of resuming the last one |

### `planner_send`

Type text into the planner's session like a paste, then press Enter.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `text` | string | yes | what to type into the planner, sent like a paste |
| `enter` | boolean | no | press Enter after the text (default true) |

### `planner_start`

Start the workspace planner's Claude Code session. It is an error if it already runs; use planner_restart then.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

## prompt

### `prompt_get`

Read the planner or session prompt of a workspace: the template in effect, the default, whether it is customised, and the variables you can use.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |

| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `kind` | string | yes | planner, session, handoff or handoff_planner |

### `prompt_render`

Show a prompt as a session would receive it, with the workspace's columns, rules, integrations and policy filled in. Pass template to preview text that is not saved yet.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |

| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `kind` | string | yes | planner, session, handoff or handoff_planner |
| `card` | string | no | render as this card's session sees it (id, nickname or key); default is a sample card for the session prompt |

Go back to Hadron's default planner or session prompt.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |

| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `kind` | string | yes | planner, session, handoff or handoff_planner |

### `prompt_set`

Replace the planner or session prompt of a workspace. It applies to sessions that start afterwards. Variables Hadron does not know are kept as written, and listed in the warning.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |

| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `kind` | string | yes | planner, session, handoff or handoff_planner |

## question

### `question_answer`

Answer an open question with the labels of the chosen options and optional notes. The user may always answer. The planner may answer under the planner policy. A session can never answer a question, least of all its own.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `question_id` | string | yes | the question id |
| `selections` | array | no | the labels of the chosen options |
| `notes` | string | no | free text that goes with the answer, or the whole answer when no option fits |

### `question_ask`

Ask the user a question about your card: a decision (with options and your recommendation), an unblock, or an approval (with what it touches, who it runs as, whether it can be undone, and the command). The card moves to Needs you until it is answered.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card` | string | no | the card; a session asks about its own card and may leave this out |
| `kind` | string | yes | decision, unblock or approval |
| `text` | string | yes | the question |
| `context` | string | no | what the reader needs to know to answer |
| `options` | array | no | the choices, each with a label and a description; put your recommendation first |
| `multi` | boolean | no | allow picking more than one option |
| `approval` | object | no | required for kind approval: what is being approved |

### `question_get`

Get one question with its options, approval details and answer. A session polls this to see whether its question has been answered.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `question_id` | string | yes | the question id |

### `question_list`

List questions, newest first, optionally for one card or one status (open, answered, withdrawn).

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `card` | string | no | only this card's questions (id, nickname or key) |
| `status` | string | no | open, answered or withdrawn |

### `question_withdraw`

Withdraw an open question that no longer needs an answer. The session that asked it, the planner and the user may withdraw it.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `question_id` | string | yes | the question id |
| `reason` | string | no | why it no longer needs an answer |

## rule

### `rule_create`

Create a rule: when a trigger happens and the optional CEL condition holds, run the actions. Triggers: field_changed{field}, column_entered{column}, card_created, report{kind}, question_opened, question_answered, idle_for{minutes}, cron{spec}. Actions: move{column_id|role|to}, set_field{path,value}, notify{text}, tell_planner{text}, run_action{script,action}. One event lets rules run at most 10 actions per card.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `name` | string | yes | what the rule does, in a few words |
| `trigger` | object | yes | when the rule runs |
| `condition` | string | no | a CEL expression that must hold for the card, such as card.assignee == 'You' |
| `actions` | array | yes | what the rule does, in order |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | default true |

### `rule_delete`

Delete a rule. The two built-in rules cannot be deleted; switch them off with rule_update.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rule_id` | string | yes | the rule id |

### `rule_dry_run`

Report what the rules would do to the board right now, without applying anything: a list of {card, rule, action, from, to}. It tries every rule that watches a field or a column against the cards as they are; rules that wait for an event, a report, a question, idle time or the clock are not simulated.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `rule_id` | string | no | only report what this rule would do |

### `rule_list`

List a workspace's rules in the order they run. Each has a trigger, an optional CEL condition and actions. The two built-in rules move a card to Needs you when a question or gate opens, and back when it closes.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `rule_log`

List what rules did lately, newest first: each firing with the card, the before and after, and each skip with its reason (a loop guard stop, a failing condition, run_action).

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `limit` | number | no | how many entries, newest first (default 50) |

### `rule_reorder`

Set the order rules run in. Pass every rule id of the workspace.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `rule_ids` | array | yes | every rule id of the workspace, in the new order; rules run in this order |

### `rule_update`

Change a rule. A built-in rule can only be switched on or off with enabled.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rule_id` | string | yes | the rule id |
| `name` | string | no | new name |
| `trigger` | object | no | new trigger |
| `condition` | string | no | new CEL condition, or an empty string for none |
| `actions` | array | no | new actions |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | switch the rule on or off |

## script

### `script_approve`

Approve a script: its tests must pass, then it runs with the permissions its manifest lists. The user may always approve. The planner may unless the planner policy is decisions_only or ask_for_prd and the script asks for network access, an MCP server or a binary that nothing approved already has. A card session never approves.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration or script name |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

Switch an enabled script off (it keeps its files and links), or reject a pending one.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration or script name |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `script_list`

List the scripts visible to a workspace (its own and the global ones) with status (pending, enabled, disabled, rejected), permissions, what they ask for that nothing approved has, test results, settings and whether each secret is set. Secret values are never returned.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `script_logs`

What scripts did lately, newest first: each op run with its duration, whether it worked, the error if not, and the lines the code logged. Secret values never appear.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | no | only this integration or script; empty for all |
| `limit` | number | no | how many rows, newest first; default 100 |

### `script_read_file`

Read manifest.json or index.js of a script.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration or script name |
| `path` | string | yes | manifest.json or index.js |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `script_remove`

Delete a script, its logs, its stored secrets and the links to its items. This cannot be undone through the UI; config_revert restores the files only.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration or script name |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `script_run_op`

Run one op of an enabled script for real (this uses its network access, secrets and binaries). Input and output are checked against the op's schema.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |

| `name` | string | yes | the integration or script name |
| `op` | string | yes | search, get, update, poll, actions.<name> or sessions.<list\|output\|send\|start\|stop> |
| `input` | object | no | the op's input object |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `script_scaffold`

Create a new script from a starter template, as pending. It does nothing until its tests pass and it is approved. Edit it with script_write_file.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | lowercase name, letters digits and underscores; for an integration it is also the field namespace (jira gives jira.status) |
| `template` | string | no | integration_scaffold: linear (through the Linear MCP server), jira (REST), github (the gh CLI) or empty; default empty |
| `global` | boolean | no | make it available to every workspace instead of only this one |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `script_test`

Run the script's recorded tests (manifest.tests). Each test calls an op with the network, exec and MCP answered by its fixtures, never the real thing, and compares the output with expect. The result is saved on the script.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration or script name |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `script_validate`

Check a script without running it: the manifest against its JSON Schema, the code parses, and every op the manifest declares is defined in the code.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration or script name |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `script_write_file`

Replace manifest.json or index.js of a script. The manifest is checked against its JSON Schema (every problem is listed) and the code must parse. An edit that keeps the same permissions re-runs the recorded tests and, if they pass, leaves an approved script enabled; an edit that asks for more makes it pending again and needs approval.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the integration or script name |

## session

### `session_adopt`

Bring an existing Claude Code conversation into Hadron as a new card and resume it with claude --resume, with Hadron's prompt and MCP server attached. Refused if another Hadron card already holds that conversation. Exit that conversation in its terminal first: two processes resuming one Claude Code conversation corrupt it.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `claude_session_id` | string | yes | the conversation's id from session_adoptable_list |
| `nick` | string | yes | the new card's nickname, kebab-case |
| `key` | string | no | an optional key such as ACME-508 |
| `column_id` | string | no | the column; default is the first active one |
| `start` | boolean | no | resume it right away (default true) |
| `handoff` | boolean | no | type the handoff message once it is ready (default true) |

### `session_adoptable_list`

List the Claude Code conversations on this Mac that were run in the workspace's root folder and could be brought into Hadron (read from ~/.claude/projects, or CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR), newest first: id, the first thing the user typed, when it was last active and its size. Conversations under 2 KB are skipped. Exit that conversation in its terminal first: two processes resuming one Claude Code conversation corrupt it.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `session_interrupt`

Press Ctrl-C in a card's session, which stops what Claude is doing.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card` | string | yes | the card: its id, nickname or key |

### `session_keys`

Press keys in a card's session: Enter, Escape, Tab, arrows, Backspace, Ctrl-<letter>, or single characters. Use it for menus and confirmations.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card` | string | yes | the card: its id, nickname or key |
| `keys` | array | yes | keys to press, in order: Enter, Escape, Tab, Up, Down, Left, Right, Backspace, Ctrl-<letter>, or one character |

### `session_read_screen`

Read what a card's terminal shows, as plain text: the last lines (default 60), optionally with the scrollback.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card` | string | yes | the card: its id, nickname or key |
| `lines` | number | no | how many lines from the bottom (default 60) |
| `scrollback` | boolean | no | include lines that scrolled off the top |

### `session_restart`

Stop a card's session if it runs and start it again. It resumes the last Claude conversation when that is known; fresh: true starts a new one.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card` | string | yes | the card: its id, nickname or key |
| `launch_profile` | string | no | a launch profile name or id; defaults to the card's own |
| `fresh` | boolean | no | start a new conversation instead of resuming the last one |

### `session_send`

Type text into a card's session like a paste, then press Enter. The call fails if the session is not running.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card` | string | yes | the card: its id, nickname or key |
| `text` | string | yes | what to type into the session, sent like a paste |
| `enter` | boolean | no | press Enter after the text (default true) |

### `session_start`

Start the Claude Code session of a card. It is an error if the card already has a running session; use session_restart then.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card` | string | yes | the card: its id, nickname or key |
| `launch_profile` | string | no | a launch profile name or id; defaults to the card's own |

### `session_status`

Report whether a card's session is running, its liveness (working, idle, waiting, ended), process id and terminal size.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card` | string | yes | the card: its id, nickname or key |

### `session_stop`

Hang up a card's running session. The card keeps its history; session_restart starts it again.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card` | string | yes | the card: its id, nickname or key |

## ui

### `ui_fullscreen`

Make the planner or card panel full screen, or leave full screen with an empty panel.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `panel` | string | no | planner or card to make full screen; empty to leave full screen |

### `ui_main_view`

Switch a workspace's main area between the board and the dashboard.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `view` | string | yes | board or dashboard |

### `ui_panel_collapse`

Collapse or expand the planner or card panel of a workspace.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `panel` | string | yes | planner or card |
| `collapsed` | boolean | yes | true to collapse the panel to a rail |

## update

### `check_for_update`

Ask GitHub whether a newer Hadron release exists. It downloads and installs nothing.

*reads*

No arguments.

### `get_update_status`

Report the running version, the newest release found, and the state of any update in progress.

*reads*

No arguments.

### `set_update_token`

Save a GitHub token in the login keychain, for checking a private repo. An empty token removes it.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `token` | string | no | a fine-grained GitHub token with Contents: read-only on the Hadron repo; empty removes the saved token |

### `start_update`

Download the newest release, verify its checksum and code signature, then quit and swap the app. If the new version does not start within 20 seconds, the old one comes back.

*changes data*

No arguments.

## view

### `view_apply`

Evaluate a saved view against the board now and return it with the ids of the matching cards. The UI keeps the active view itself.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view_id` | string | yes | the view id |

### `view_delete`

Delete a saved view.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view_id` | string | yes | the view id |

### `view_list`

List a workspace's saved filter views in order.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `view_save`

Save the current filter (pinned values, text search, CEL expression) as a named view. The expression must compile. Saving under an existing name replaces that view.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `view_id` | string | no | update this view; without it, a view with the same name is replaced, else a new one is created |
| `name` | string | yes | the view's name |
| `filters` | object | yes | the filter to save |

## widget

### `widget_pin`

Pin a widget from a chat to the dashboard as a custom block. Pinning the same widget twice returns the block that already exists.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message_id` | string | yes | the id of a widget message from chat_read |
| `title` | string | no | the block's heading; default is the widget's title |

### `widget_post`

Post a small HTML widget (a table, a chart, a status board) on a channel. The planner, the user, or a session on its own card may post. It is stored now and rendered in a sandboxed frame later.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
| `channel` | string | yes | planner, or card:<card id, nickname or key> |
| `title` | string | yes | a short title for the widget |
| `html` | string | yes | the widget as HTML; it renders in a sandboxed frame with no network |

## workspace

### `workspace_archive`

Archive a workspace so it leaves the tab bar, or restore it with archived: false. Nothing is deleted.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | the workspace id |
| `archived` | boolean | no | true (default) to archive, false to restore |

### `workspace_create`

Create a workspace with its columns, the built-in rules, the default dashboard and prompts. The first workspace becomes the active one.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the workspace name, up to 60 characters |
| `root` | string | no | the root folder; ~ is expanded. Defaults to the home folder |
| `color` | string | no | a #rrggbb colour; defaults to the next swatch |
| `template` | string | no | column template: planner (default), simple or copy |
| `copy_from` | string | no | with template copy, the workspace whose columns to copy |
| `integrations` | array | no | integration ids to enable |

### `workspace_delete`

Delete a workspace and everything in it: columns, cards, chats, rules, dashboard. This cannot be undone; prefer workspace_archive.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | the workspace id |

### `workspace_get`

Get one workspace by id, with its integrations, filter bar and UI state.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | the workspace id |

### `workspace_import_planner_dir`

Import an older planner's run folder into a workspace: sessions/<nick>.md become cards (with their reports and planner messages and the Claude session id to resume), log.md sets each card's column (planning and in-progress go to the first active column with that stage, backlog to backlog, done to done), questions/<nick>/Q-NN.json become questions and gates/<nick>.json become gates. Cards are created without starting; session_start resumes the conversation with claude --resume. Nicknames that already exist are skipped, so importing twice changes nothing. dry_run (the default) only returns the plan.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace to import into; defaults to the active one |
| `dir` | string | no | the planner run folder; default is <workspace root>/.ai/runs/planner |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | only report the plan and change nothing (default true). Pass false to import |

### `workspace_list`

List workspaces in order. Archived ones are left out unless include_archived is true.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `include_archived` | boolean | no | also list archived workspaces |

### `workspace_switch`

Make a workspace the active one. Actions that omit workspace_id then act on it.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | the workspace id |

### `workspace_update`

Change a workspace's name, root folder, colour, enabled integrations or pinned filter fields. Only the fields you pass change.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | yes | the workspace id |
| `name` | string | no | new name |
| `root` | string | no | new root folder |
| `color` | string | no | new #rrggbb colour |
| `integrations` | array | no | the enabled integration ids |
| `filter_bar` | array | no | the field paths pinned in the filter bar |

## worktree

### `worktree_list`

List the git worktrees Hadron made for cards (launch profiles with worktree on), with their branch and whether they have uncommitted changes. Worktrees of deleted cards are listed too: card_delete leaves them on disk.

*reads*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |

### `worktree_remove`

Remove a card's git worktree. Refused while the tree has uncommitted changes (unless force is true) or while the card's session is running. The branch hadron/<nick> stays, so committed work is kept.

*changes data*

| Argument | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `card` | string | yes | the card (id, nickname or key), or the nickname of a deleted card whose worktree was left on disk |
| `force` | boolean | no | remove it even with uncommitted changes. They are lost; the branch keeps what was committed |
| `workspace_id` | string | no | the workspace; defaults to the active one |
